summary: rjust returns a string padded on the left until it reaches a minimum width.
documentation: rjust returns a string padded on the left until it reaches a minimum width. If text is already at least that wide it is returned without truncation. The fill character must be exactly one character.
inputs: An object with text (string) and width (integer from 0 to 30).
returns: Text left-padded with spaces to the requested minimum width.
caution: Width counts Python string characters, not terminal display columns; combining marks and wide glyphs can display differently. This exercise uses ASCII.
scenarios: Align quantities in a plain-text inventory export.
Format right-aligned totals in a fixed-width receipt.
Prepare a column of ASCII labels for an older printer.
title: Align a report column
problem: Input is {text, width}, using ASCII text and width 0..30. Return text right-aligned to that minimum width using spaces. Never cut off longer text.
goal: Use str.rjust() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Call rjust with its default space fill.
